models._description: Adds usage='base_automation' and base_automation_id link; the server action is the executable body of a rule
action_open_automation delegation helper for the time-based scheduler cron

behavioral_notes.observation: The engine's core trick, invisible to ORM metadata. _register_hook() searches all base.automation rules and, for each rule's model_name, monkey-patches the live class in env.registry: create (CREATE_TRIGGERS), write + _compute_field_value (WRITE_TRIGGERS), unlink (on_unlink), message_post (mail triggers), and injects per-rule methods into Model._onchange_methods (on_change). Each patched method stores method.origin = the previous implementation, calls it, then routes affected records into automation._process(). patch() guards against double-patching a model/method. _unregister_hook() deletes the patched attributes. _update_registry() (invoked from base.automation create/write/unlink when CRITICAL_FIELDS change) re-installs the patches and sets registry_invalidated = True so other workers reload. Net effect: creating one automation rule rewires the create/write/unlink of an UNRELATED model (e.g. sale.order, crm.lead) at runtime with no static dependency.

Rules carry two safe_eval domains. make_write() snapshots old_values for stored fields in vals, evaluates filter_pre_domain against records BEFORE the super() write (so a rule can require 'was unpaid before this edit'), runs the original write, then evaluates filter_domain (post) against the survivors; only matching records reach _process. on_create_or_write rules derive trigger_field_ids from the domain fields, and _check_trigger_fields() compares record[name] to old_vals to skip records whose watched fields did not actually change. filter_pre_domain is never checked on create. This pre/post split is pure code semantics, not derivable from field metadata.

_process() is the single execution path: it subtracts records already handled (context '__action_done' dict keyed automation -> recordset) to stop recursive/duplicate firing when an action's own writes re-trigger the same rule, stamps date_automation_last when present, builds an active_model/active_id/active_ids context per record, then for every linked action_server_ids calls action.with_context(**ctx).run() under sudo. The actual side-effect (send mail, add follower, schedule activity, run Python, update fields) lives in the ir.actions.server record, so base_automation supplies trigger+condition wiring while ir.actions.server supplies the effect. Exceptions pass through _add_postmortem (attaches rule id/name for the error dialog) and re-raise.

Time triggers (on_time / on_time_created / on_time_updated) are NOT hooked into create/write; the cron 'base_automation.ir_cron_data_base_automation_check' scans them. _cron_process_time_based_actions() iterates active TIME_TRIGGERS rules, calls _search_time_based_automation_records(until=now) which computes a relative date window from last_run, trg_date_range, trg_date_range_mode (before/after) and trg_date_range_type, optionally honouring trg_date_calendar_id working days via calendar.plan_days, runs _process per matched record, flushes, writes last_run=now and _commit_progress() per rule (rollback + continue on error). _update_cron() auto-activates the cron and shrinks its interval to ~10% of the smallest rule delay (floor 1 minute, ceiling 4 hours) whenever rules change.

Two non-store entry points. (1) on_webhook rules expose a public /web/hook/<uuid> route; _execute_webhook() safe_evals record_getter against the JSON/query payload to resolve the target record, optionally logs to ir.logging, then calls _process. (2) on_change registers per-rule onchange methods so rules fire live in the form view; the frontend ships an ActionsOne2ManyField OWL component, base_automation_trigger_selection / base_automation_actions_one2many field widgets, a GroupConfigMenu patch + 'open_automations' group_config_items entry, and a base_automation error_dialog registry handler that renders the _add_postmortem rule context. None of this UI wiring or webhook record-resolution is visible in Python ORM metadata.

it_architecture.application: base_automation (Automation Rules engine — event-condition-action triggers that monkey-patch target models and fire ir.actions.server)
logical_data_erm: base.automation -> ir.model (model_id, the watched target model)
information_flows: depends: base, digest, resource, mail, sms
hook: base.automation.create/write/unlink -> _update_registry -> _register_hook patches target Model.create/write/unlink/_compute_field_value/message_post + Model._onchange_methods at runtime

trigger: target record create/write/unlink/onchange -> patched method -> _filter_pre/_filter_post (safe_eval domains) -> _process -> ir.actions.server.run (mail/followers/activity/code/field-update side-effects)
webhook: external HTTP POST -> /web/hook/<uuid> -> _execute_webhook -> record_getter safe_eval -> _process
loop-guard: context __action_done dict de-duplicates records across re-entrant writes
frontend_components: ActionsOne2ManyField (OWL one2many widget editing the rule's server actions inline)
base_automation error_dialog (renders _add_postmortem rule id/name on action failure)

capabilities: React to Record Lifecycle Events (create / write / unlink / archive / field-set)
Evaluate Pre- and Post-Update Conditions (filter domains)
Schedule Time-Based Automations (date-field / after-creation / after-update, calendar-aware)
Fire Live UI On-Change Automations (form-view reactivity)
Ingest Inbound Webhooks (public /web/hook endpoint with record resolution)
Execute Linked Server Actions (mail, followers, activities, Python code, field updates)
value_streams: Rule-to-Effect: configure rule -> _register_hook patches target model -> event fires -> condition filter -> server action runs
Time-to-Effect: configure timed rule -> cron scan window -> matched records -> server action runs
Webhook-to-Effect: external POST -> record_getter resolves record -> condition -> server action runs
information_concepts: ir.actions.server (the executable action body, extended here)
organization: base.group_system (Settings) — sole access group on base.automation config
policies: Rules ARE the policy layer: ECA triggers express 'when X happens and condition Y holds, do Z' across any model

_check_trigger / _check_trigger_state / _check_action_server_model constraints enforce valid trigger-action combinations (on_change requires code action; on_unlink forbids mail/activity actions; action model must match rule model)
filter_pre_domain is not evaluated on create
stakeholders: Business administrator / functional consultant (authors automation rules, no code)
Developer (writes Python-code server actions and record_getter logic)
Integrator (configures inbound webhooks from third-party apps)
End user (indirectly affected as rules mutate the records they edit)
metrics: ir.logging webhook call log (log_webhook_calls) viewable via action_view_webhook_logs

classification.rationale: base_automation is a cross-cutting workflow-automation framework — firm IT infrastructure with no business object of its own (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). Its single real model, base.automation, holds rule definitions, not business documents; the actual work is _register_hook monkey-patching ANY target model's create/write/unlink at runtime and dispatching ir.actions.server. It does not itself create value in a chain/shop/network — it is the trigger plumbing other primary modules (sale, crm, project...) bolt onto, which is why category is 'Sales/Sales' yet application=false and auto_install=false. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits because base_automation is business-process-automation tooling — develop/deliver and operate application logic (ECA rules, scheduled jobs, webhook integration) as an IT capability. 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was considered because automation rules arguably configure business behaviour; rejected because base_automation is a concrete running engine (a workflow runtime + scheduler + webhook endpoint), i.e. IT solution delivery/operation, not the governance/portfolio/change-management capability 13.0 covers. The work is building and running automation software, which is squarely 8.0.

standard_capabilities: No-code event-condition-action rules on any model (create/write/unlink/archive/stage/tag/state/priority/user-set)
Pre-update and post-update domain conditions with old-value diffing
Time-based triggers (date field, after creation, after last update) with before/after delay and working-calendar support
Live on-change (UI) automations bound to specific fields
Inbound webhook trigger (/web/hook/<uuid>) with configurable record_getter and optional call logging
Mail triggers (on incoming / outgoing message) for mail-thread models
Delegation to ir.actions.server effects: send email, add followers, schedule activity, execute Python, update fields
typical_fits: Auto-assign salesperson / set follower / send confirmation when a record reaches a stage
Reminder activity N days before/after a date field via the time scheduler
Webhook from a third-party app updating an Odoo record on external events
Field-derived defaults / validations via on_change code automations
common_gaps: Complex multi-step or branching workflows (beyond a flat list of server actions) need custom Python actions or a dedicated workflow module
Ordering/priority between competing rules on the same model is implicit
Heavy on_time rules can pressure the shared cron interval (auto-shrinks to as low as 1 minute)
Recursive automations need careful design despite the __action_done guard
Outbound integrations are not provided here (gap #7: 0 HTTP call sites) — only inbound webhook + ir.actions.server effects

open_questions: Exact set of downstream modules that ship default base.automation rules vs. those authored by customers at runtime (registry patching is dynamic).
Performance envelope of broad write triggers (no trigger_field_ids) on high-volume models.
Interaction/ordering when multiple rules patch the same model method and one action's writes re-trigger another rule.
Real row counts unavailable (runtime extraction empty) — rule population is per-deployment.
